options: A fixed-size array decided at compile time
A growable, ordered list of values of the same type
A lookup table that finds values by key
quiz.explain: Vec<T> is a growable, ordered list. You add to the end with .push() and index from 0.

quiz.q: What happens with `v[99]` when the vector only has 3 items?
options: It panics at runtime with 'index out of bounds'
It grows the vector to 100 items
quiz.explain: Indexing out of bounds panics. Use v.get(99), which returns an Option, when the index might not exist.

quiz.q: How do you find a value in a `HashMap` by its key?
options: By its numeric position, like map[0]
You can't look up individual keys
By looping until you reach the right index
quiz.explain: A HashMap is keyed, not positional. .get(key) returns Some(value) if the key exists, or None if it doesn't.

quiz.q: Why does `let scores = Vec::new(); scores.push(10);` fail to compile?
options: Vec::new() is not a real function
push needs the vector to be declared `let mut`
You must specify the type as Vec<i32>
quiz.explain: push modifies the vector, so it must be mutable: `let mut scores = Vec::new();`.

flashcards.front: What is a Vec<T> and how do you add to it?
flashcards.back: A growable, ordered list of same-typed values. Add to the end with .push(); index from 0. Must be `let mut` to modify.

flashcards.front: How do you safely read an index that might not exist?
flashcards.back: Use .get(i), which returns Option (Some or None). Plain v[i] panics if the index is out of bounds.

flashcards.front: What is a HashMap<K, V> for?
flashcards.back: Looking up values by a key you choose. Add pairs with .insert(key, value); read with .get(key). Remember `use std::collections::HashMap;`.

flashcards.front: How do you print a whole Vec or HashMap?
flashcards.back: Use the debug placeholder {:?}, e.g. println!("{:?}", v). Plain {} only works for single simple values.
